cards.text: Jesus goes with His disciples to a place called Gethsemane. He tells them, "Sit here while I go over there and pray." Friend, lean in close, because this one is heavy.
He takes three disciples with Him: Peter and the two sons of Zebedee, James and John. Then something changes in Jesus.

cards.question: Jesus walks on with Peter, James and John. What does He begin to feel?

cards.text: Then Jesus says it out loud to them: "My soul is consumed with sorrow to the point of death."

cards.question: Jesus is consumed with sorrow. What does He ask Peter, James and John to do?

answers.text: Stay and keep watch with Him
Go back and wake the others
Head into the city for help

cards.text: He goes a little farther, falls facedown and prays, "My Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass from Me."

cards.question: Jesus prays for this cup to pass from Him. But in that same prayer, whose will does He put first?
Jesus comes back to the disciples He asked to keep watch with Him. What does He find them doing?

cards.text: Jesus asks Peter, "Were you not able to keep watch with Me for one hour?" And look, I can't judge, friend: I once fell asleep right next to my own oven timer while it was BEEPING.

cards.question: Jesus tells the sleepy disciples, "Watch and pray so that you will not enter into temptation." What reason does He give?

answers.text: The spirit is willing but the body is weak
The night is long but the morning is near
The enemy is strong but you are stronger

cards.text: A second time He goes away and prays, "My Father, if this cup cannot pass unless I drink it, may Your will be done."

cards.question: When Jesus comes back the second time, He finds the disciples awake and watching.
The disciples' eyes are heavy, so Jesus leaves them and prays a ___ time, saying the ___ thing.

cards.text: Then He comes back to the disciples and says, "Are you still sleeping and resting? Look, the hour is near, and the Son of Man is betrayed into the hands of sinners."

cards.question: Jesus tells the disciples, "Rise, let us go!" What does He see coming?

cards.text: While Jesus is still speaking, Judas arrives. Judas is one of the Twelve, and he did NOT come alone.

cards.question: Judas shows up while Jesus is still speaking. Who is with him?

answers.text: A large crowd with swords and clubs

cards.question: The armed crowd with Judas was sent from the chief priests and elders of the people.

cards.text: Now Judas, the betrayer, had arranged a signal with the crowd ahead of time. That way they'd arrest the right man.

cards.question: What signal did Judas set up so the crowd would know which one to arrest?

cards.text: Judas walks straight up to Jesus. "Greetings, Rabbi!" he says, and he kisses Him.

cards.question: Judas has just kissed Jesus. What does Jesus call Judas when He answers him?

cards.text: "Friend," Jesus replies, "do what you came for." Then the men step forward, seize Jesus and arrest Him.

cards.question: When the men seize Jesus, nobody with Him tries to fight back.
One of Jesus' companions draws his sword and strikes the servant of the high priest. What does the sword cut off?
Jesus speaks to the companion who swung the sword. What does Jesus tell him to do with it?

answers.text: Put it back in its place
Hand it over to the crowd

cards.text: Jesus tells him, "For all who draw the sword will die by the sword." Then Jesus asks if he knows what help is just one call to the Father away.

cards.question: Jesus says He can call on His Father. What would the Father put at His disposal at once?

answers.text: More than twelve legions of angels

cards.text: More than twelve LEGIONS of angels! Friend, it only took ONE angel to get me out of the back of a junk drawer.

cards.question: Jesus could call on all those angels. So why doesn't He?

answers.text: So the Scriptures would be fulfilled
Because the angels were too far away
Because the crowd was too large

cards.text: Then Jesus speaks to the crowd: "Have you come out with swords and clubs to arrest Me as you would an outlaw?" Swords? CLUBS? Like He's been hiding somewhere?

cards.question: Jesus reminds the crowd that He sat teaching in the temple courts every day, and they did not arrest Him.

cards.text: Jesus tells them, "But this has all happened so that the writings of the prophets would be fulfilled."

cards.question: Earlier on the Mount of Olives, all the disciples said they would never deny Jesus. Now He's been arrested. What do all the disciples do?

answers.text: They stand and fight the crowd

cards.text: And that's where we'll leave it for now. Trust me, friend, this story is NOT over.

findings.problem: The card names the two sons of Zebedee as James and John. That fact isn't in the passage (it comes from Matthew 4:21 and 10:2), and the card gives no reference for it. The card cites only Matthew 26:37.

rule.text: **References.** Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates the stop: 6 of the 8 choice cards are multiple choice (cards 3, 5, 7, 8, 10 and 15). There is only 1 true or false and 1 fill in the blank.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates the stop: 8 of the 11 choice cards are multiple choice, 3 are true or false, and there is no fill in the blank. The mix leans heavily on multiple choice, like stop 1.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: Several story cards are only a BSB quote with no Papa Dorin voice or framing: stop 1 cards 4, 6, 11 and 14, and stop 2 card 18. They read as stripped-down Scripture readouts, not a storyteller carrying the moment.

rule.text: **Short, but not stripped down.** A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: Both wrong answers echo John's account of this same arrest. John 18:3 describes a detachment of soldiers and officers carrying torches. A baker who knows John could argue that 'A few guards carrying torches' or 'Roman soldiers' is right.

rule.text: **No near-matches.** A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: The story card only repeats the answer to card 13 (more than twelve legions of angels) and adds a joke. It tells no new part of the passage. The joke should ride on a card that moves the passage forward.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The right answer stands out. It is the only answer phrased 'So the Scriptures...' while both wrong answers start with 'Because...', and it is the only one that sounds biblical. 'Because the angels were too far away' also contradicts the 'at once' the baker just learned, so it's barely believable.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The question brings in a fact from outside the passage: earlier, on the Mount of Olives, all the disciples said they would never deny Jesus (Matthew 26:30, 35). It gives no reference for that fact.

rule.text: **References.** Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: The line that says the story isn't over copies the doc's example almost word for word. Only 'is NOT' replaces 'is not'.

rule.text: The examples show the idea. Write your own line each time.
